correctness.rationale: An independently written exhaustive computation, replay with python3 /workspace/audit_a6.py, gives all seven class rows, including both 72-element 5-cycle classes. It closes the permutation groups under positive words (which suffice in a finite group), then obtains each derived step by normally closing the generator commutators, not by copying the supplied all-commutator routine. The normal closure equals the derived group because the quotient makes the generators commute; exact equality at a nontrivial derived step certifies nonsolubility. Conjugation transports each representative's complete partner list to each class element. The exact length vectors at 0,1,2,3,infinity are identity (1,359,0,0,0), either order-three type (0,9,54,27,270), double transposition (0,8,128,32,192), either 5-cycle class (0,5,5,0,350), and type (4,2) (0,4,68,32,256). Cyclic normalizers are 360,18,8,10,8 in those respective grouped rows, so only 18 fails to divide the applicable sum (63). No finite length beyond three occurs. Totals (1,2519,16920,6480,103680) give the fractions 3/20 and 1/5. For each length-three subgroup I verified a faithful action on its four cyclic order-three subgroups, proving isomorphism to S4, and reconstructed the counts of actual generating pairs for all 30 subgroups (216 each). Every copy of S4 is generated by a pair (for example, a 4-cycle and an adjacent transposition), and has derived length three, so this covers all copies. The frozen checker alone tests only one subgroup's 216 count and does not explicitly implement the prose's isomorphism test; the independent calculation closes both gaps. No conclusion about other alternating groups or every classwise threshold is needed.

value.rationale: The group and length threshold are motivated independently by the published failure of the proposed divisibility extension. Exact localization to two classes answers where it fails, and the complete pair census identifies precisely the S4 contribution separating the metabelian probability 3/20 from the soluble probability 1/5. These are usable exact checks for bounded solubilizer and random-generation calculations, more than repeating an existence example or an ATLAS table.
